refs.title: Egyptian Building (Medical College of Virginia), 1200 block of East Marshall Street, Richmond Independent City, Virginia
refs.note: The survey number is printed on the data page's own cover, twice ('EGYPTIAN BUILDING HABS VA-1421 (Medical College of Virginia) VA-1421'). THE DATA FILE IS A COVER SHEET ONLY: its whole content is that title block plus 'PHOTOGRAPHS PAPER COPIES OF COLOR TRANSPARENCIES'. There is no written historical and descriptive data to quote, which is why this record carries no `survey` block.

refs.title: Medical College of Richmond (now Egyptian Building, Medical College of Virginia) by Thomas S. Stewart
refs.note: Describes 'The battered walls of the structure seem like the pylons of ancient Egyptian temples', 'the open lotus bud capitals', 'the reliefs depicting the solar disk with the cobra, and the cavetto cornice', and the cast-iron fence whose 'posts are mummies--or herms, as one source calls them (Brownell 270) and intermittent obelisks'. It also calls the building five-storeyed with 'relatively minimal windows'.

note: Seeded 5 Sep 2026, WP-11.3 Tranche 2, the mid-nineteenth-century city house cluster. A HABS item exists for the finest surviving American Egyptian Revival building and it is photographs and colour transparencies with a one-page cover -- no dimensions, no bays, no description. The style node's exemplar note ('Battered walls, distyle in antis porticoes with palm capitals, flanking obelisks joined by a cast-iron fence with hermai') is corroborated in detail by the Bluffton College page, EXCEPT the capitals: that page and the Downtown Presbyterian survey both say LOTUS BUD where the node says PALM. Recorded here; the node is not edited.
